post.caption:
Cooking is pre-digestion. Heat breaks down tough structure before it reaches you, so cooked food releases far more usable calories for far less chewing and gut work. Great apes spend most of their waking hours chewing; we spend under an hour a day eating. Human guts are small for our body size and our brains are huge, and both are metabolically expensive. The fossil record shows the trade happening: guts shrink, skulls grow, teeth get smaller. No other animal cooks.
